agent.title: Let an agent do it
agent.intro: Paste this into Claude Code, Cursor or another coding agent, from the root of your Mood Kit repository. It makes the agent read the rules first.
agent.secretsNote: An agent should never see real secrets. Keys, passwords and tokens go into your environment by hand, and accounts, DNS and payments are yours to create. Details in Working with agents.

seo.title: Vue and Nuxt SaaS Boilerplate with a Laravel API
seo.description: Laravel + Nuxt SaaS starter kit: multi-tenant workspaces on subdomains with Postgres row-level security, roles, Stripe billing, notifications and an admin.
seo.ogTitle: Mood Kit: Laravel + Vue/Nuxt SaaS starter kit

landing.h1: A Vue and Nuxt SaaS boilerplate with a Laravel API and tenant isolation in the database
landing.lead: Mood Kit is a Laravel 13 API and a Nuxt 4 app on mood-ui. Nuxt is Vue 3 with routing and server rendering on top, so if you write Vue you already know the frontend. Each customer gets a workspace on its own subdomain, and Postgres row-level security keeps their rows apart even when a query forgets a filter. Sign-in, roles, plans, Stripe billing, notifications, onboarding, team, clients and a platform admin are already built and tested.
landing.pricingNote: One payment, lifetime updates, as many projects as you want.
landing.factsTitle: What it is, in four lines

facts.api: A Laravel 13 JSON API, versioned under /api/v1, with one response envelope and a code for every error.
facts.app: A Nuxt 4 frontend built from Nuxt layers, with server rendering and the mood-ui components.
facts.tenancy: Workspaces on subdomains, one database, row-level security on every tenant table.
facts.checks: Architecture rules enforced by Deptrac, Pest and ESLint, so the code stays the shape the docs describe.

landing.forBody: Teams that are building a B2B product where each customer is an organization with its own people, roles, plan and data: a booking tool, a CRM, a back office, a vertical SaaS. It also suits agencies that build the same kind of product for several clients, and Laravel developers who want a separate Vue front end instead of Inertia.
landing.notForBody: If you want a landing page and a login for a weekend MVP, a lighter Nuxt template will get you there sooner. If you want a single-user app with no workspaces, the tenancy layer is more than you need.
landing.includedLead: Everything below exists in the kit today and has a documentation page.

tenancy.title: Multi-tenancy with row-level security
tenancy.text: Workspaces on acme.yourdomain.com. The tenant is set per database session and enforced by Postgres policies, with a runtime role that cannot bypass them. A command fails the deploy if it can.

auth.title: Sign-in and workspace switching
auth.text: Bearer-token login across subdomains, password reset, a captcha with Cloudflare Turnstile, and moving between the workspaces a person belongs to.

rbac.title: Roles, permissions and the menu
rbac.text: Roles and permissions per workspace, role templates, a permission middleware and a menu that follows what the person may do.

billing.title: Plans, quotas and Stripe Billing
billing.text: A catalog of plans with quota limits and feature flags, checkout, plan changes, the Customer Portal and a webhook, plus an admin editor for the catalog.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.text: Event types, templates per language, an in-app inbox with live updates, email deliveries with bounce handling, and daily digests.

onboarding.title: Onboarding and workspace templates
onboarding.text: A wizard and a checklist for a new workspace, steps your modules can add, and templates a workspace starts from.

team.title: Team, branches and clients
team.text: Invitations, working hours and skills; branches on a map with opening hours; clients with tags, duplicate merging, CSV import and export, privacy rights and a client portal.

platform.title: A platform admin on its own host
platform.text: Super admins on admin.yourdomain.com: workspaces, plans, signup mode, impersonating a member, and an audit trail nobody can edit.

brand.title: Brand per workspace
brand.text: Each workspace sets its name, logo and colors, and each member picks a theme. The platform has its own brand for emails and public screens.

ops.title: The production plumbing
ops.text: Queues and a scheduler, Reverb for realtime, Sentry with secrets scrubbed, S3 or R2 storage, and a checklist with the commands to run on every deploy.

landing.stackLead: Nothing exotic. You can read every layer.

database.name: Database
database.value: PostgreSQL with row-level security, Redis for cache and queue

storage.name: Storage and mail
storage.value: S3-compatible (MinIO, Cloudflare R2); SMTP, SES, Postmark or Resend

quality.name: Quality gates
quality.value: Pint, Deptrac, Larastan, Rector, ESLint, Vitest, Playwright, gitleaks

agents.name: For agents
agents.value: AGENTS.md with the rules, enforced by those gates

template.q: Is this a Nuxt SaaS template or a complete application?
template.a: A complete application. It has an API, a Nuxt frontend, a database schema, background jobs and a test suite. It is not a landing page template. If you want a marketing site with pricing and docs, Nuxt UI ships a free one, and it works well beside this.

why.q: Why a Laravel API with Nuxt and not Inertia?
why.a: Because the API stands on its own: a mobile app or another client can use it, and the frontend deploys separately. The cost is two things to deploy. The docs cover the part people struggle with, authentication across subdomains, which uses bearer tokens instead of cookies.

isolation.a: All workspaces share one database. Every tenant table has a row-level security policy, the app connects as a role that cannot bypass it, and php artisan tenancy:verify-rls fails the deploy if the setup could let rows leak. A forgotten where clause does not show another customer's data.

requirements.q: What do I need to run it?
requirements.a: Node 22 or 24 with pnpm 10, PHP 8.4 with a few extensions, Composer 2 and Docker. Docker runs Postgres, Redis, Mailpit and MinIO. Getting started takes about 15 minutes, most of it installing dependencies.

agents.q: Can I build on it with Claude Code or Cursor?
agents.a: Yes, that is a design goal. AGENTS.md at the repository root holds the rules, and each rule names the check that enforces it. The docs have a prompt for each common task and say which steps an agent can do alone and which need you.

license.q: How is it licensed and delivered?
license.a: One payment of 149 USD, or 99 USD with the launch discount for the first 100 buyers. You can use it in as many of your own and your clients' projects as you want, and every future version is included. You get read access to the private GitHub repository and a license key, both from Polar right after paying.
